setupNotes:
Start: `pnpm start`

Setup: copied .env.example to .env and set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET to a generated hex value. NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is left empty, so auth uses the request's origin; open the app at http://localhost:<port> for passkeys. RESEND_API_KEY is unset, so in production confirmation and reminder mail cannot be sent (no outbox outside dev). `pnpm build` succeeded (.output); `pnpm db:migrate` created a fresh .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db. `pnpm start` runs `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs`, which loads .env itself. Run it from /tmp/judge-CdHInD/app. NOT SEEDED: the db:seed task is dev-only (/_nitro/tasks/db:seed returns 404 in production). Seeding through the rubric's rsync dev copy failed: with node_modules symlinked, Vite reports "Failed to load url .../nitro/dist/runtime/internal/vite/dev-entry.mjs". So the database is empty (GET /api/events returns total 0). Create accounts through sign-up in the UI, or seed it some other way. The seed would create ada/grace/linus @meetups.test with password meetups-demo-password. Note: `pnpm start` spawns a node child. Killing the pnpm PID leaves node listening, so stop the node process (check `ss -ltnp`). All servers I started are stopped. The agent's patch removes defineCachedFunction from server/api/events/[slug]/index.get.ts entirely, so each request computes going/isOrganizer per user with no cache.

Scripted checks (already graded; don't grade them again):
- F1: pass. organizer isOrganizer=true; other isOrganizer=false going=false; signed out isOrganizer=false going=false; other RSVPs (200), then other going=true; third going=false isOrganizer=false.
- C2: pass. Seats left was 20 before the RSVP and 19 right after.

The patch changes only server/api/events/[slug]/index.get.ts, the event route that held the cache. It does not touch the page or any component.
The agent removed defineCachedFunction and now computes the whole response on each request. Dropping the cache is one of the two forms of the best solution.
Nothing in the route is cached any more. `going` and `isOrganizer` come from getSessionUser(event) on each request, so no cached value depends on the visitor.
The patch only deletes code inside one route. It adds no store, cache service, table or dependency.
The cache is removed, not given a shorter maxAge, and the API itself now returns the correct per-user `isOrganizer` and `going`. There is no client-side workaround.
No cache is left in the route: the defineCachedFunction import and its wrapper were removed, and no hand-written Map or KV cache was added.

vibe.summary: The agent found the cause: `defineCachedFunction` was keyed only by slug but returned per-user `going` and `isOrganizer`. It fixed it by removing the cache completely, so the diff is small, clean and in one file. A reviewer would ask to keep the shared event data cached by slug and work out the per-user fields outside the cache, and would want a test with two sessions.

findings.why: It finds the real cause: per-user `going` and `isOrganizer` were stored in a cache keyed only by slug. Now both come from the request's own session, so one user's answer can no longer be shown to another.
findings.text: It finds the real cause: per-user `going` and `isOrganizer` were stored in a cache keyed only by slug. Now both come from the request's own session, so one user's answer can no longer be shown to another.

findings.why: The diff stays small and in one file. The existing `Promise.all` query shape is kept, and the now-unused `nitro/cache` import is removed, so nothing from the old version is left behind.
findings.text: The diff stays small and in one file. The existing `Promise.all` query shape is kept, and the now-unused `nitro/cache` import is removed, so nothing from the old version is left behind.

findings.why: The fix deletes the whole `defineCachedFunction` instead of only taking the per-user fields out of it. The event row, organizer name and seat count were shared by every visitor and could stay cached, so every page view now runs the queries again.
findings.fix: Keep `defineCachedFunction(..., { name: "event-page", maxAge: 60, getKey: slug => slug })` for the public payload only (event fields, organizerName, seatsLeft). In the handler, call `getSessionUser(event)`, then add `going: user ? await isGoing(id, user.id) : false` and `isOrganizer` on top of the cached result.

findings.why: The diff has no test showing that two different sessions get different `going` and `isOrganizer` values for the same slug, so nothing stops someone from adding back a slug-keyed cache around user data.
findings.fix: Add a small server test (for example `@nuxt/test-utils` `$fetch` with two signed-in Better Auth sessions) that requests `/api/events/:slug` as the organizer and then as another user, and checks `isOrganizer` and `going` for each.

findings.why: The response mixes public and private data but sets no cache header. The sibling seats and attendees routes say their caching policy, but this one leaves it to any CDN or route rule added later, and that could bring the same leak back at the HTTP layer.
findings.fix: Set `event.res.headers.set("cache-control", "private, no-store")` (as `attendees.csv.get.ts` does), or split the personal fields into their own endpoint so the public payload can be cached safely.
